To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the clinical problem of a growing pelvic tumour in androgen-independent prostate carcinoma can only be solved by a combination of radical surgery and radiotherapy.
the natural history of androgen-independent prostate carcinoma (AIPC) is not uniform, but that it is determined by the site of the tumour, i.e. the presence or absence of a symptomatic pelvic mass.

patients with symptomatic AIPC and pelvic-confined disease have a median survival of 19 months after pelvic RT, while the median survival for patients with pelvic disease and distant metastases or painful bone metastases is 9 months and 8 months, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the detection of the prostate cancer.
the development of novel therapeutic strategies for prostate cancer patients.
the clinical problem of a growing pelvic tumour in AIPC patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
palliative RT is a valuable treatment modality for AIPC patients with a symptomatic tumour in the pelvis.
the palliation of AIPC patients with pelvic tumours and distant metastases remains to be improved.

palliative RT in AIPC patients is a valuable tool in the management of patients with symptomic pelvic tumour, whereas the role of palliative RT in patients with painful bone metastasis remains to be defined in prospective studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the natural history of AIPC is not only influenced by the extent of disease but also by the site of the disease.
patients with symptomatic AIPC and pelvis-confine disease should be treated by a combined approach of surgical debulking of the pelvic tumour and radiotherapy.
palliative RT in AIPC patients can be a very effective treatment modality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the natural course of AIPC is different depending on the clinical presentation and that the clinical presentation should be accounted for in future trials of AIPC.
patients with symptomatic, pelvic-confined disease have a much better prognosis than patients with symptomatic disease and distant metastases.
the clinical problem of symptomatic AIPC patients with pelvic tumours is different from the clinical problem of AIPC patients with painful bone metastasis and should be considered as such.
